exercises.questionText:
MC If all measurements are in cm, the area of the figure is:
The figure is bounded by three semicircles along a straight line of length $7 + 3 = 10\text{ cm}$: a large semicircle of diameter $10\text{ cm}$ below the line, a medium semicircle of diameter $7\text{ cm}$ (on the left part of the line) curving down inside it and removed, and a small semicircle of diameter $3\text{ cm}$ (on the right part of the line) added above the line.
A. $16.49\text{ cm}^2$  B. $39.25\text{ cm}^2$  C. $9.81\text{ cm}^2$  D. $23.56\text{ cm}^2$

steps: Given: semicircles with radii $5$, $3.5$ and $1.5\text{ cm}$. Goal: the area of the figure.
$A = 23.56\text{ cm}^2$ (2 d.p.), which is option D.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the figure is $23.56\text{ cm}^2$; the answer is D.
solution.tip: Decide which semicircles are added and which are cut away before calculating.

exercises.questionText:
MC If all measurements are in centimetres, the area of the figure is:
The figure is a rectangle $6\text{ cm}$ wide and $5 + 5 + 5 = 15\text{ cm}$ tall. Its right-hand side is divided into three $5\text{ cm}$ sections: semicircles of diameter $5\text{ cm}$ are cut out of the top and bottom sections, and a semicircle of diameter $5\text{ cm}$ is added outward on the middle section.
A. $50.73\text{ cm}^2$  B. $99.82\text{ cm}^2$  C. $80.18\text{ cm}^2$  D. $90\text{ cm}^2$

steps: Given: rectangle $6 \times 15$; semicircles with $r = 2.5\text{ cm}$. Goal: the area.
Net effect: two removed, one added, so one semicircle is lost overall.
$A = 90 - 9.817... = 80.18\text{ cm}^2$ (2 d.p.), which is option C.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the figure is $80.18\text{ cm}^2$; the answer is C.
solution.tip: Identical pieces added and removed cancel, which can save calculation.

exercises.questionText:
MC If all measurements are in centimetres, the shaded area of the figure is:
The shaded figure is a ring with inner radius $2\text{ cm}$ and outer radius $7\text{ cm}$, with a $30^\circ$ sector cut out.
A. $3.93\text{ cm}^2$  B. $11.52\text{ cm}^2$  C. $388.77\text{ cm}^2$  D. $129.59\text{ cm}^2$

solution.formula: Area of an annular sector: $A = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi(R^2 - r^2)$
steps: Given: $r = 2$, $R = 7$, gap $30^\circ$ so $\theta = 330^\circ$. Goal: the shaded area.
$A = 129.59\text{ cm}^2$ (2 d.p.), which is option D.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the shaded area is $129.59\text{ cm}^2$; the answer is D.
solution.tip: Here the 7 is measured from the centre, so it is the outer radius.

exercises.questionText:
MC The total surface area of the solid is:
The solid is a hemisphere of radius $28\text{ mm}$ on top of a cone with the same radius and slant height $40\text{ mm}$.
A. $8444.6\text{ mm}^2$  B. $9221\text{ mm}^2$  C. $14\,146.5\text{ mm}^2$  D. $50\,271.1\text{ mm}^2$

solution.formula: Hemisphere curved area $= 2\pi r^2$; cone curved area $= \pi rl$
steps: Given: $r = 28\text{ mm}$, $l = 40\text{ mm}$. Goal: the total surface area.
$\text{TSA} = 8444.6\text{ mm}^2$ (1 d.p.), which is option A.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area is $8444.6\text{ mm}^2$; the answer is A.
solution.tip: The flat circle where the two parts meet is inside the solid, so it is not counted.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the following plane figure (all measurements in cm): a triangle with base $12$ and perpendicular height $14$.

solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the triangle is $84\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: Use the dashed perpendicular height, not a sloping side.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the following plane figure (all measurements in cm): a trapezium with parallel sides $10$ and $15$ and perpendicular height $8$.

solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the trapezium is $100\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: The arrows on the sides show which two sides are parallel.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the following plane figure (all measurements in cm), correct to 2 decimal places: a triangle with sides $3$, $7$ and $5$.

solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the triangle is $6.50\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: With only side lengths given, Heron's formula is the tool to use.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the following plane figure (all measurements in cm), correct to 2 decimal places: an ellipse with semi-major axis $6$ and semi-minor axis $3$.

steps: Rounded to 2 decimal places: $56.55\text{ cm}^2$ (using $\pi = 3.14$ gives $56.52\text{ cm}^2$)
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the ellipse is $56.55\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: Use the calculator's $\pi$ key for the most accurate answer.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the following plane figure (all measurements in cm): a rhombus with diagonals $10$ and $12$.

solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the rhombus is $60\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: The dashed lines are the diagonals, not sides.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the following plane figure (all measurements in cm), correct to 2 decimal places: a circle of radius $10$ with an $80^\circ$ sector removed.

steps: Given: $r = 10$, gap $80^\circ$, so $\theta = 280^\circ$. Goal: the area.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the shape is $244.35\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: Subtract the missing angle from $360^\circ$ first.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the following figure (all measurements in cm): a rectangle $20$ long and $15$ high with a semicircle of diameter $15$ cut out of its left end and an identical semicircle added to its right end.

solution.formula: Area of a rectangle: $A = lw$ (the semicircles cancel)
steps: Given: rectangle $20 \times 15$; equal semicircles removed and added. Goal: the area.
The semicircle removed on the left equals the semicircle added on the right, so they cancel.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the figure is $300\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: Look for pieces that can be moved to make a simple shape.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the following figure (all measurements in cm), correct to 2 decimal places: a rectangle $12$ wide and $10$ high, with a semicircle of diameter $12$ on top and a triangle of base $12$ and height $8$ below.

steps: Given: rectangle $12 \times 10$, semicircle $r = 6$, triangle $b = 12$, $h = 8$. Goal: the area.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the figure is $224.55\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: The dashed 12 cm line is the diameter of the semicircle.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the area of the following figure (all measurements in cm): a shape with a bottom edge of $20$ and a left edge of $10$. The top edge runs $10$ from the top-left corner, then a sloping edge goes down to the right to a point $5$ above the bottom, then a horizontal edge of $6$ runs to the right, and the right edge drops $5$ to the bottom.

solution.formula: Area = rectangle $-$ removed rectangle $-$ removed triangle
steps: Given: bounding rectangle $20 \times 10$. Goal: the area.
Removed rectangle at top right: $6$ wide and $10 - 5 = 5$ high: $6 \times 5 = 30\text{ cm}^2$
Removed triangle under the slope: horizontal leg $20 - 10 - 6 = 4$, vertical leg $5$: $\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 5 = 10\text{ cm}^2$
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the figure is $160\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: Work out the missing lengths from the given ones before splitting the shape.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the blue shaded area (all measurements in cm), correct to 2 decimal places: a circle with centre O and radius $QO = 15\text{ cm}$. Triangle PQR is inscribed in the circle with base $PR = 18\text{ cm}$; its height QS passes through O, with S on PR and $SO = 8\text{ cm}$. The shaded region is the circle outside the triangle.

steps: Given: $r = 15$, $PR = 18$, $QS = QO + OS = 15 + 8 = 23$. Goal: the shaded area.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the shaded area is $499.86\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: The triangle's height runs from Q all the way to S, so add QO and OS.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the blue shaded area (all measurements in cm), correct to 2 decimal places: a quarter circle of radius $12.5$ with the chord joining the ends of its arc drawn; the shaded region is the segment between the chord and the arc.

steps: Given: $r = 12.5$. Goal: the shaded segment area.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the shaded area is $44.59\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: Both legs of the triangle are radii, so both equal 12.5.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the blue shaded area (all measurements in cm), correct to 2 decimal places: six circles of radius $5$, arranged in 2 rows of 3, fit exactly inside a rectangle; the shaded region is the rectangle outside the circles.

steps: Given: $r = 5$, so each diameter is 10. Rectangle $= 3 \times 10$ by $2 \times 10$, i.e. $30 \times 20$. Goal: shaded area.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the shaded area is $128.76\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: Find the rectangle's size from the number of diameters along each side.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the total surface area of the solid, correct to 2 decimal places: a closed cylinder with radius $35\text{ cm}$ and height $50\text{ cm}$.

solution.formula: TSA of a cylinder: $\text{TSA} = 2\pi r(r + h)$
steps: Given: $r = 35\text{ cm}$, $h = 50\text{ cm}$. Goal: the TSA.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area is $18\,692.48\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: Include both circular ends for a closed cylinder.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the total surface area of the solid, correct to 2 decimal places: a cone with base radius $14\text{ mm}$ and slant height $20\text{ mm}$.

solution.formula: TSA of a cone: $\text{TSA} = \pi r(r + l)$
steps: Given: $r = 14\text{ mm}$, $l = 20\text{ mm}$. Goal: the TSA.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area is $1495.40\text{ mm}^2$.
solution.tip: The 20 mm is along the sloping side, so it is the slant height $l$.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the total surface area of the solid, correct to 2 decimal places: a sphere with radius $8\text{ cm}$.

solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area is $804.25\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: Surface area uses $r^2$; volume uses $r^3$.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the total surface area of the solid, correct to 2 decimal places: a triangular prism of length $18\text{ cm}$ whose triangular ends are isosceles with two equal sides of $14\text{ cm}$ and a third side of $12\text{ cm}$.

solution.formula: TSA = 2 triangular ends + perimeter × length; triangle height by Pythagoras
steps: Given: triangle sides $14$, $14$, $12$; length $18$. Goal: the TSA.
Height of triangle onto the 12 cm side: $h = \sqrt{14^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{196 - 36} = \sqrt{160} = 12.649...\text{ cm}$
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area is $871.79\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: In an isosceles triangle the height bisects the unequal side, so use half of 12 in Pythagoras.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the total surface area of the solid, correct to 2 decimal places: a cylinder of diameter $14\text{ mm}$ and length $10\text{ mm}$ with a smaller cylinder of diameter $4\text{ mm}$ and length $10\text{ mm}$ attached centrally to one end [closed at both ends].

solution.formula: Cylinder parts: circle $\pi r^2$, curved surface $2\pi rh$
steps: Given: large $R = 7$, length 10; small $r = 2$, length 10 (mm). Goal: the exposed surface area.
The small cylinder covers $\pi \times 2^2 = 4\pi$ of one large end, but its own far end ($4\pi$) is exposed, so these cancel.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area is $873.36\text{ mm}^2$.
solution.tip: The covered circle and the small cylinder's end have the same area, so they cancel.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the total surface area of the solid: a cube of edge $10\text{ cm}$ with a square-based pyramid of perpendicular height $12\text{ cm}$ on top (the pyramid's base is the top face of the cube).

solution.formula: TSA = 5 cube faces + 4 triangles; slant height by Pythagoras
steps: Given: edge $10\text{ cm}$, pyramid height $12\text{ cm}$. Goal: the TSA.
Slant height of each face: $l = \sqrt{12^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{144 + 25} = \sqrt{169} = 13\text{ cm}$
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area is $760\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: The slant height uses half the base edge (5 cm) and the vertical height (12 cm).

exercises.questionText: Calculate the volume of a cube with edge length $7\text{ cm}$.

solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume of the cube is $343\text{ cm}^3$.
solution.tip: $7 \times 7 = 49$, then $49 \times 7 = 343$.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the volume of a rectangular prism $12\text{ cm}$ long, $8\text{ cm}$ wide and $7\text{ cm}$ high.

solution.formula: Volume of a rectangular prism: $V = lwh$
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume of the prism is $672\text{ cm}^3$.
solution.tip: Multiply all three dimensions.

exercises.questionText: Calculate the volume, correct to 2 decimal places, of a cylinder with radius $35\text{ cm}$ and height $40\text{ cm}$.

solution.formula: Volume of a cylinder: $V = \pi r^2 h$
steps: Given: $r = 35\text{ cm}$, $h = 40\text{ cm}$. Goal: the volume.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume of the cylinder is $153\,938.04\text{ cm}^3$.
solution.tip: Square the radius before multiplying by the height.

exercises.questionText: Determine the volume, correct to 2 decimal places, of a half-cylinder with diameter $1\text{ m}$ and length $3.7\text{ m}$.

solution.formula: Volume of a half-cylinder: $V = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^2 h$
steps: Given: $r = 0.5\text{ m}$, $h = 3.7\text{ m}$. Goal: the volume.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume is $1.45\text{ m}^3$.
solution.tip: The cross-section is a semicircle, so halve the cylinder volume.

exercises.questionText: Determine the volume of a triangular prism whose triangular cross-section has base $12\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $10\text{ cm}$, and whose length is $30\text{ cm}$.

solution.formula: Volume of a triangular prism: $V = \frac{1}{2}bh \times H$
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume of the prism is $1800\text{ cm}^3$.
solution.tip: Find the triangle's area first, then multiply by the length.

exercises.questionText: Determine the volume, correct to 2 decimal places, of a cone with base radius $10\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $12\text{ cm}$.

solution.formula: Volume of a cone: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume of the cone is $1256.64\text{ cm}^3$.
solution.tip: Don't forget the $\frac{1}{3}$ for a cone.

exercises.questionText: Determine the volume of a square-based pyramid with base side $9\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $11\text{ cm}$.

steps: Given: base $9 \times 9 = 81\text{ cm}^2$, $H = 11\text{ cm}$. Goal: the volume.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume of the pyramid is $297\text{ cm}^3$.
solution.tip: The 11 cm is the vertical (dashed) height, so it can be used directly.

exercises.questionText: Determine the volume of a rectangular-based pyramid with base $42\text{ cm}$ by $20\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $30\text{ cm}$.

steps: Given: base $42 \times 20 = 840\text{ cm}^2$, $H = 30\text{ cm}$. Goal: the volume.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume of the pyramid is $8400\text{ cm}^3$.
solution.tip: $\frac{1}{3}$ of 30 is 10, which makes the multiplication easy.

exercises.questionText: Determine the volume, correct to 2 decimal places, of a sphere with radius $12\text{ mm}$.

solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the volume of the sphere is $7238.23\text{ mm}^3$.
solution.tip: Cube the radius: $12^3 = 1728$.

exercises.questionText: A rectangular block of land $4\text{ m} \times 25\text{ m}$ is surrounded by a concrete path $1\text{ m}$ wide. Calculate the area of the path.

solution.formula: Path area = outer rectangle $-$ inner rectangle
steps: Given: block $4 \times 25$, path 1 m wide. Goal: path area.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the area of the path is $62\text{ m}^2$.
solution.tip: Add the path width to both sides of each dimension.

exercises.questionText: A concrete path around a block of land has an area of $62\text{ m}^2$. Determine the cost of concreting at $\$45$ per square metre.

steps: Given: area $62\text{ m}^2$, rate $\$45$ per $\text{m}^2$. Goal: the cost.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the cost of concreting is $\$2790$.
solution.tip: Check units: $\text{m}^2 \times \$/\text{m}^2$ gives dollars.

exercises.questionText: If the radius is tripled and the height of a cylinder is divided by six, then determine the effect on its volume (in comparison with the original shape).

solution.formula: Volume of a cylinder: $V = \pi r^2 h$
steps: Given: new radius $3r$, new height $\frac{h}{6}$. Goal: compare volumes.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore $V_{\text{new}} = \frac{3}{2}\pi r^2 h$: the volume will be 1.5 times as large as the original volume.
solution.tip: Tripling the radius multiplies the volume by $3^2 = 9$.

exercises.questionText: If the length is halved, the width is tripled and the height of a rectangular prism is doubled, then determine the effect on its volume (in comparison with the original shape).

solution.formula: Volume of a rectangular prism: $V = lwh$
steps: Given: new dimensions $\frac{l}{2}$, $3w$, $2h$. Goal: compare volumes.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore $V_{\text{new}} = 3lwh$: the volume will be 3 times as large as (triple) the original volume.
solution.tip: Multiply the three scale factors together.

exercises.questionText: A cylinder of radius $14\text{ cm}$ and height $20\text{ cm}$ is joined to a hemisphere of radius $14\text{ cm}$ to form a bread holder. Calculate the total surface area, correct to 2 decimal places.

solution.formula: TSA = circular base + cylinder curved surface + hemisphere: $\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2$
steps: Given: $r = 14\text{ cm}$, $h = 20\text{ cm}$. Goal: the TSA.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area is $3606.55\text{ cm}^2$.
solution.tip: The joined faces are hidden, so only one flat circle is counted.

exercises.questionText: The bread holder (cylinder radius $14\text{ cm}$, height $20\text{ cm}$, joined to a hemisphere of radius $14\text{ cm}$) has a total surface area of $1148\pi \approx 3606.55\text{ cm}^2$. Determine the cost of chroming the bread holder on the outside at $\$0.05$ per $\text{cm}^2$.

steps: Given: area $3606.548...\text{ cm}^2$, rate $\$0.05$ per $\text{cm}^2$. Goal: the cost.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore chroming the bread holder costs $\$180.33$.
solution.tip: Round money to the nearest cent at the end.

exercises.questionText: A cylinder of radius $14\text{ cm}$ and height $20\text{ cm}$ is joined to a hemisphere of radius $14\text{ cm}$ to form a bread holder. Calculate the storage volume of the bread holder, correct to 2 decimal places.

steps: Given: $r = 14\text{ cm}$, $h = 20\text{ cm}$. Goal: the volume.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the storage volume is $18\,062.06\text{ cm}^3$.
solution.tip: Use a common denominator to add the two $\pi$ terms exactly.

exercises.questionText: The new bread holder has a storage volume of $\frac{17\,248\pi}{3} \approx 18\,062.06\text{ cm}^3$. Determine how much more space is in this new bread holder than the one it is replacing, which had a quarter circle end with a radius of $18\text{ cm}$ and a length of $35\text{ cm}$. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

solution.formula: Prism volume $V = AH$ with quarter-circle area $A = \frac{1}{4}\pi r^2$
steps: Given: old holder quarter-circle end $r = 18\text{ cm}$, length $35\text{ cm}$. Goal: the extra space.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the new bread holder has $9155.65\text{ cm}^3$ more space.
solution.tip: The old holder is a prism with a quarter-circle cross-section.

exercises.questionText: Bella Silos has two rows of silos for storing wheat. Each row has 16 silos and all the silos are identical, with a cylindrical base (height of $5\text{ m}$, diameter of $1.5\text{ m}$) and conical top (diameter of $1.5\text{ m}$, height of $1.1\text{ m}$). Calculate the slant height of the conical tops, correct to 2 decimal places.

steps: Given: cone $r = 0.75\text{ m}$, $h = 1.1\text{ m}$. Goal: slant height $l$.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the slant height of each conical top is $1.33\text{ m}$.
solution.tip: Use the radius (half the diameter) in Pythagoras.

exercises.questionText: Bella Silos has 32 identical silos (2 rows of 16), each with a cylindrical base (height $5\text{ m}$, diameter $1.5\text{ m}$) and a conical top (diameter $1.5\text{ m}$, height $1.1\text{ m}$, slant height $\approx 1.3314\text{ m}$). Determine the total surface area of all the silos, correct to 2 decimal places.

solution.formula: Each silo: base circle $\pi r^2$ + cylinder curved $2\pi rh$ + cone curved $\pi rl$
steps: Given: $r = 0.75\text{ m}$, $h = 5\text{ m}$, $l = 1.3314...\text{ m}$, 32 silos. Goal: total surface area.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the total surface area of all the silos is $910.91\text{ m}^2$ (including their bases).
solution.tip: Multiply the area of one silo by the number of silos ($2 \times 16 = 32$).

exercises.questionText: Bella Silos has 32 identical silos, each with a cylindrical base (height $5\text{ m}$, radius $0.75\text{ m}$) and a conical top (radius $0.75\text{ m}$, slant height $\approx 1.3314\text{ m}$). Evaluate the cost of painting the silos if one litre of paint covers $40\text{ m}^2$ at a bulk order price of $\$28.95$ per litre.

steps: Given: the bases sit on the ground and are not painted. Goal: cost of paint.
If only whole litres can be bought: 22 L, costing $22 \times \$28.95 = \$636.90$
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore painting the silos costs $\$618.35$, or $\$636.90$ if you have to buy 22 full litres.
solution.tip: The base of each silo sits on the ground, so it is not painted.

exercises.questionText: Bella Silos has 32 identical silos, each with a cylindrical base (height $5\text{ m}$, diameter $1.5\text{ m}$) and a conical top (diameter $1.5\text{ m}$, height $1.1\text{ m}$). Determine how much wheat can be stored altogether in these silos, correct to 2 decimal places.

steps: Given: $r = 0.75\text{ m}$; cylinder $h = 5$, cone $h = 1.1$; 32 silos. Goal: total volume.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore the silos can store $303.48\text{ m}^3$ of wheat altogether.
solution.tip: Volume uses the vertical height of the cone (1.1 m), not the slant height.

exercises.questionText: The 32 silos hold $303.48\text{ m}^3$ of wheat. Wheat is pumped from these silos into cartage trucks with rectangular containers $2.4\text{ m}$ wide, $5\text{ m}$ long and $2.5\text{ m}$ high. Determine how many truckloads are necessary to empty all the silos.

solution.formula: Truck volume $V = lwh$; truckloads = total $\div$ truck volume, rounded up
steps: Given: total $303.48\text{ m}^3$; truck $2.4 \times 5 \times 2.5$. Goal: number of truckloads.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore 11 truckloads are necessary to empty all the silos.
solution.tip: 10 trucks leave some wheat behind, so round up.

exercises.questionText: A cartage truck container is $2.4\text{ m}$ wide, $5\text{ m}$ long and $2.5\text{ m}$ high. If wheat is pumped out of the silos at $2.5\text{ m}^3/\text{min}$, determine how long it will take to fill one truck.

steps: Given: truck volume $= 2.4 \times 5 \times 2.5 = 30\text{ m}^3$; rate $2.5\text{ m}^3/\text{min}$. Goal: time.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore it takes 12 minutes to fill one truck.
solution.tip: Divide the volume by the flow rate; check the units cancel to minutes.

exercises.questionText: The Greek mathematician Eratosthenes developed an accurate method for calculating the circumference of the Earth 2200 years ago. In the figure, C is the centre of the Earth, A is the town of Alexandria and S is the town of Syene, exactly $787\text{ km}$ due south. When the sun's rays (parallel lines) were vertical at Syene (so the ray through S passes through C), they formed an angle of $7.2^\circ$ at Alexandria ($\angle BVA = 7.2^\circ$), obtained by placing a stick VA at A (pointing along CA extended) and measuring the angle formed by the sun's shadow with the stick. Assuming that the sun's rays are parallel, evaluate the angle $\angle SCA$, correct to 1 decimal place.

solution.formula: Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal
steps: Given: $\angle BVA = 7.2^\circ$; the ray at V and the ray through S and C are parallel. Goal: $\angle SCA$.
The line CAV crosses both parallel rays (a transversal).
$\angle BVA$ and $\angle SCA$ are alternate angles, so they are equal.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore $\angle SCA = 7.2^\circ$.
solution.tip: Look for a 'Z' shape formed by the two parallel lines and the transversal.

exercises.questionText: In Eratosthenes' method, $\angle SCA = 7.2^\circ$ at the centre C of the Earth. Given that the arc $AS = 787\text{ km}$, determine the radius of the Earth, SC. Write your answer correct to the nearest kilometre.

solution.finalAnswer: Therefore Eratosthenes' method gives the radius of the Earth as $6263\text{ km}$.
solution.tip: $7.2^\circ$ is $\frac{1}{50}$ of a full turn, so the circumference is 50 times the arc.

exercises.questionText: Eratosthenes' method gave the radius of the Earth as $6263\text{ km}$. Given that the true radius is $6380\text{ km}$, determine Eratosthenes' percentage error, correct to 1 decimal place.

steps: Given: estimate $6263\text{ km}$, true $6380\text{ km}$. Goal: percentage error.
solution.finalAnswer: Therefore Eratosthenes' percentage error was $1.8\%$.
solution.tip: Divide the error by the true value, not by the estimate.
